name: Sterling
description: A design system for data-dense applications: design tokens, a Figma library, and matching React components, built from one set of definitions.
summary: Sterling is a design system for data-dense applications: design tokens, a Figma library generated by a plugin, and matching React components in Storybook, all built from one set of definitions.

files.contains: 24 components and the 20 icons: what each is for, when to use it, its Figma properties, its React props, and its links.
Every token in the Design Tokens (DTCG) format: colors in Light and Dark, spacing, sizes, the three densities, and the text styles, each with its CSS name.
7 guideline sections (the rules) and 9 patterns (complete compositions with numbered steps).

package.name: sterling-ui
package.note: Not on a package registry: npm installs it from the GitHub Release. It needs React 19 or newer.
package.stylesNote: Import styles.css once: it holds the tokens (--stl-… custom properties), the text style classes (.stl-text-…), and every component's CSS. fonts.css loads Inter.
package.components: import { Button, DataGrid, type Column, type GridRow } from "sterling-ui";
package.types: Every component has a props type named after it (ButtonProps). The declarations are in the package's dist/types folder.
package.colorMode: Follows the operating system. To set it, put data-theme="light" or data-theme="dark" on the root element.
package.density: Default unless a parent has the class stl-density-compact or stl-density-comfortable.

howToUse: Choose components from components.json: match the task to `description`, `useWhen`, and `dontUseWhen`. Use only components and icons that are listed; Sterling has no others.
Follow a component's `related` entries into guidelines.json (by `id`) for the rules and patterns that apply to it.
Build screens from the patterns in guidelines.json. Each pattern says when to use it and explains its parts step by step.
In code, import the React component from the package (`react.import`) and use the props under `react`. Prop values are the strings listed; there is no `state` prop (see `states`).
Style only with tokens from tokens.dtcg.json, through the CSS custom property or class named in each token's $extensions. Never write a raw color, size, or font value.
Use the semantic color tokens (color.*), never the primitives, and never rely on color alone for meaning: pair it with an icon, a sign, or a label.
All sample data in Sterling is fictional. Keep it that way in anything generated from these files.

sections.title: MCP server
text: Sterling includes a small read-only MCP server that answers questions about its components, tokens, guidelines, and patterns from this same export. It runs on your machine over stdio and makes no network requests. It is one self-contained file, `server.js`, with the export inside it: copy it anywhere and run it with Node.js 20 or newer. Nothing else needs installing. It isn't published to a package registry: to build the file, clone the repository, then run `npm install` and `npm run build` in `mcp/`, which writes `mcp/dist/server.js`.
Connect it to Claude Code with `claude mcp add sterling -- node /path/to/server.js`. In any other MCP client, add a stdio server whose command is `node` with that file as its argument.
Tools: list_components, get_component, get_tokens, get_token, list_guidelines, get_guideline, get_pattern, search.
